newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Socialists urge EU public works spending.
newsitem.headline: French Socialists urge EU public works spending.

text.p: Acting French Socialist party head Francois Hollande said on Monday the European Union should use existing EU structural and investment funds to back job-creating public works programmes, and possibly increase those funds.
Hollande told a press briefing that whatever emerged from an EU summit in Amsterdam would only be a step in making jobs a permanent feature of EU talks alongside monetary concerns.

He was speaking amid signs of a possible agreement at the EU summit where French Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin is fighting for a jobs pact alongside the "stability pact" on deficit control after the launch of the euro single currency.

"We want three concrete advances," Hollande said, stressing that he was speaking for the Socialist Party and not France's left-wing government, which is Socialist-dominated but also comprises Communists and Greens.

"The first is coordination of economic policy in a way that allows for policy oriented towards growth, and which acts as a counterweight to the (future) European Central Bank, which must be seen as an instrument of stability -- that's sure -- but at the service of economic policy coordination aimed at jobs and growth," Hollande said.
"The danger is not that inflation will take off again. The danger -- and it's not even a threat or a danger, but a reality -- is unemployment," he told reporters.

"The second advance is an employment chapter (in the Maastricht treaty) -- that means making an employment criterion, an employment goal, a permanent feature of discussions in Europe. There must also be a jobs pact," he said.

"The third dimension is a policy geared to the economic situation which must provide a stimulus through a number of major works projects which can be financed by the European Investment Bank," he said.
"On this point, I must add that it is not a new innovation, since the idea was already contained in the conclusions to the Essen (EU) summit in 1994," he said.
"It's a pity that the governments which came before us in France and Europe did not pay the attention needed for these major works projects to start up," he said.
"(But) this whole process does not end at Amsterdam. There will be other rendezvous afterwards, whatever the outcome in Amsterdam," he said.
"The social dimension amounts to the ability to spell out social norms at the European level, on the minimum wage, work conditions and protection vis-a-vis layoffs," he said.

"We (the EU) are putting procedures in place related to budget criteria. Should there not also be a jobs criterion which says that when unemployment is worsening, Europe should commit itself to trying out an economic policy aimed at fighting unemployment -- that we are not simply bound by budgetary criteria?" he said.

"We want there to be big works projects. There are funds which can be exploited. The structural funds exist and can be increased. That's moreover what (former European Commission President) Jacques Delors had planned in 1994," Hollande said.
"There are also investment funds, the European Investment Bank. A certain number of financing sources can be called on," he said.
